A nonprofit virtual assistant coordinates a programme deadline

In this fictional example, a nonprofit is preparing a volunteer event while a grant opportunity comes up for review.

A donation needs an acknowledgement and a member asks about renewing. Donor and member administration gives each item a record and an owner without mixing contact details, event logistics and grant decisions in one inbox.

  1. 01

    Check the donor and member records

    Use the approved CRM fields to record the donation or renewal request and confirm the source and contact preference. Donor and member administration can prepare the acknowledgement or reply using the current template. Flag a duplicate or uncertain permission before adding someone to a campaign.

  2. 02

    Coordinate the event and open assignments

    A nonprofit virtual assistant can maintain the volunteer roster, check signups and gaps, and send the approved reminders. Record the next action for any unfilled shift or outstanding vendor item. Keep costs, safety questions and public statements with the programme lead.

  3. 03

    Prepare a sourced grant review packet

    Use grant research support to check the funding source, published criteria, deadline and required documents. Link the original guidance and gather the materials already approved for review. Put questions about eligibility, budget and programme claims in the decision list for the grant owner.

Set up donor and member administration

Before the first batch, give the assistant one routine example and one item that needs a decision. Compare both with the instructions to see which rules are already clear and which need to be written down.

Donor and member administration rules

Provide the permitted CRM fields, consent and contact preferences, approved acknowledgement wording and who can change a record. Share an example of a donation and an incomplete renewal. Agree which details belong in a restricted workspace and which can appear in a status report.

Volunteer and event operating notes

Give the nonprofit virtual assistant the event schedule, roles, capacity and backup contact. Confirm which communications the assistant can send and which changes need approval. Document the route for an unfilled shift, cancellation or late change to the venue.

Grant research support checklist

List priority programmes, geographic or other inclusion criteria, approved sources and the internal owner for each opportunity. Define the evidence needed for a review pack and who decides whether to apply. Identify the person who can approve programme descriptions, budgets and submissions.

Decide what happens when the normal rule fails.

Record the source, what you checked and who can decide. Keep blocked work visible until the next action changes.

Two contacts look like the same donor

Donor and member administration can link the potential match and document how the records differ. Keep preferences and transaction references intact until the authorised owner decides whether to merge. Pause an acknowledgement or campaign update if the destination or consent is uncertain.

A volunteer shift is uncovered

The nonprofit virtual assistant can check the approved backup list and share available options with the event owner. If the change affects the programme or a participant commitment, ask for approval before sending updates. Record who was contacted and which coverage is still pending.

A deadline or criterion is unclear

Grant research support can record the exact question, published source and date, and ask the grant owner to confirm the next action. Keep unverified eligibility or budget claims out of the draft submission. Record who will clarify the point and by when.

Review grant research support and programme records

Use a few completed items and one unresolved case. Confirm what the next owner can tell from the record, then agree one change to test during the next cycle.

Check records and acknowledgement status

Sample a donation, a renewal and an open exception. Confirm the source record, approved contact preference and whether the intended communication was drafted, approved or sent. Donor and member administration should leave the next owner visible without exposing unnecessary details.

Review event readiness

Ask the nonprofit virtual assistant to show confirmed volunteers, unresolved shifts, vendor commitments and the timing of the next update. Compare a sample with the source roster. Check that access to personal details is limited to the people who need them for the event.

Verify grant evidence before review

For grant research support, compare the deadline, requirements and materials with the original funding source. Confirm the reviewer can tell which records are verified and what still needs a programme or finance decision. Keep any approved changes with the evidence.

Leave a record the next person can use.

Give the next nonprofit virtual assistant the programme calendar and donor and member administration queue. List owners for volunteer changes, public updates and grants.

Plan coverage for events, renewals and grant research support

A routine member queue and an event week have different deadlines. Set review dates around the points when a programme, finance or board owner needs to act.

Routine member and donor work

Choose when donor and member administration checks new records, renewals and acknowledgements. Give the record owner a separate list of duplicates and consent questions. Keep the last approved communication visible before handing the queue to another person.

Events and volunteer peaks

Use a nonprofit virtual assistant to prepare a pre-event roster review and confirm which changes need the lead. Record the cutoffs for reminder messages, venue updates and vendor confirmations so a substitute can pick up the right item.

Funding and board deadlines

Plan grant research support around the public deadline and the internal review window. Prepare the eligibility questions, approved records and draft reporting inputs early enough for the programme and finance owners to check them. Record what changed and which version reached the board or grant reviewer.

Frequently Asked Questions

Agree who approves donor and member administration decisions and which sources to use for grant research support.

Can you maintain donor or member records?

Yes. Agree which fields and acknowledgement workflows are in scope and how to handle consent and duplicates.

Can you research grants?

We can compile sourced opportunities and deadlines, gather approved inputs and route a draft pack to your reviewer.

Can you coordinate volunteers?

We can track signups, send approved reminders and maintain rosters and shift schedules.

Can you help with events?

We can coordinate calendars, guest or participant updates, vendor follow-ups and the review checklist.

Can you help with board meetings?

We can organise agendas and pre-reads, capture agreed actions and track outstanding items.

Who approves fundraising communications?

Your authorised team approves public claims, recipients, spending, submissions and commitments.
